subject: Hosted API quickstart — onramp plan and temporary SLA exception request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@avaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API quickstart — onramp plan and temporary SLA exception request

Hi Maya — thanks again for the demo call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary from today
- Goal: Pilot Redwood Hosted API for Ava Retail’s checkout personalization service (recommendations + short summarization).
- Primary constraints you mentioned: sensitive PII in some logs, expected steady-state traffic (~30 RPS) with short bursts to ~150 RPS, streaming websocket usage for live typing in ~10% of calls, latency SLO target ~150ms p50.

Redwood recommended path
1) Start with a 2-week hosted pilot (sandbox + staging endpoints) so we can validate latency and token cost against live traffic.
2) We can provision elevated temporary rate caps for the pilot (see proposed mapping below) but will need a short SLA exception signed by Revenue Ops.
3) If you need strict network separation or specific residency controls, we’ll evaluate Dedicated or Private (VPC) afterward — we can do that transition with pinned model versions and preserved prefix cache to avoid retraining caches.

For the pilot we’ll deliver:
- Sandbox endpoints + credentials (sandbox-credentials-AVR.txt)
- SOC2 summary and data handling docs (Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf)
- Mutual Action Plan (mutual_action_plan_AVR.xlsx) with milestones and acceptance criteria

Asks from your side (so we can finalize the M.A.P.)
- Confirm expected average QPS and peak burst duration (e.g., 150 RPS for <5 minutes vs sustained)
- Confirm what fraction of calls will use streaming vs standard responses
- Any hard compliance constraints (data residency, retention windows, masking) that would force Private from day 1

Proposed temporary pilot rate mapping
- Sandbox (testing): 250 RPS burst / 60 RPS sustained (sandbox will be throttled tight)
- Staging (pilot): 180 RPS burst / 40 RPS sustained
- Prod (if pilot passes): map to Dedicated or Hosted production quotas per contract

Next steps
- I’ll email sandbox creds once we confirm the QPS/burst numbers and finalize a short SLA exception for the pilot (one-page addendum).
- Can you loop in procurement (Tom) for any paperwork?

Thanks — I’ll wait for the QPS/burst confirmation and any compliance notes. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow up if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (summary), mutual_action_plan_AVR.xlsx (M.A.P. draft)

Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart — onramp plan and temporary SLA exception request

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

Traffic profile
- Expected average production load after initial launch: about 25–35 RPS.
- Burst profile: up to 150 RPS for traffic spikes (typical burst <10 minutes, calendar-driven sales can hit ~20 min).
- Streaming: roughly 8–12% of calls will be streaming for live typing.

Compliance
- We have PII (emails, order IDs) in some logs. We need to understand how long Redwood retains request/response logs by default and whether we can disable retention for pilot.
- Data residency: primary systems in us-west; we prefer processing in US regions.

Procurement
- I've looped Tom from procurement on this thread. He’ll take the paperwork piece. Tom, we’d like to run a hosted pilot first; procurement will advise if we need an inbound SOW.

We’re okay to start with the Hosted pilot as you suggested, provided there’s a short addendum clarifying retention and a temporary rate uplift for the trial. Can you send the SOC2 summary and the mutual action plan? Also please share sandbox creds when ready.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Product — Personalization | Ava Retail
maya@avaretail.com

- Approve a temporary rate uplift for the staging pilot: target staging mapping 180 RPS burst / 40 RPS sustained; sandbox higher for internal validation.

2) Soojin: can Revenue Ops sign off on a 30-day temporary uplift (staging) for a strategic pilot? If not, what documentation do you need (traffic profile, expected token volumes)?

I’ll prep the M.A.P. and attach the SOC2 summary once I have your green light.

— Ben

Hi Maya / Tom — thanks for the quick reply and for looping Tom in. Next steps and answers to your asks below: 

1) Retention and compliance
- We can provide a pilot configuration that disables long-term request/response retention for a named tenant. We’ll also provide a one-time purge record and a confirmation timestamp for audit. I attached the SOC2 summary which outlines our controls.

2) Temporary rate uplift and pilot quotas
- We can provision the following for the 14-day pilot: staging endpoints at 180 RPS burst / 40 RPS sustained; sandbox with a 250 RPS burst cap. If you need a second uplift (e.g., longer bursts for a sale), we can do a one-time short-duration increase after Revenue Ops sign-off.

3) SLA exception/process
- Revenue Ops has an expedited pilot exception form. Soojin — could you confirm the minimal paperwork required (I’ve cc’d you and Marissa). If approved, we’ll sign a one-page addendum that grants the temporary quotas and documents retention settings.

4) Region and streaming
- We will ensure pilot endpoints are in us-west to meet your residency preference. Streaming is supported over our websocket/stable stream endpoints; we’ll provide docs and a short sample client.

Attachments (sent): Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, mutual_action_plan_AVR.xlsx, sandbox-credentials-AVR.txt

Proposed timeline
- Today: sign off on pilot QPS/burst and retention toggle (you)
- 24–25 Jul: Revenue Ops approves exception and we provision staging/sandbox endpoints
- 26 Jul: handoff to engineering for integration and a 48–72 hour smoke test window

Tom — if you want, happy to set a 20-min procurement call to walk through the one-page addendum and the M.A.P.

Cheers,
